meta.description: Watches a folder for new hanger/fabric photos, sends each image to the Digital Textile Library /api/ingest endpoint (which runs AI extraction, uploads to Supabase Storage, saves the fabric record, logs the extraction and recalculates similar fabrics), then notifies staff when a record lands in the review queue. See docs/N8N_SETUP.md for setup and for swapping the folder source (Google Drive / Dropbox / Local / OneDrive).

nodes.name: Watch Folder (Google Drive)
nodes.notes: SOURCE NODE — swap this node to change the watched folder source. Alternatives: Dropbox Trigger, Local File Trigger (self-hosted n8n), or Microsoft OneDrive Trigger. Whatever the source, the next node only needs the file binary. Set WATCH_FOLDER_ID in n8n environment variables.

nodes.name: Download Image
nodes.notes: Downloads the new file as binary so it can be base64-encoded. If you swapped the trigger to Dropbox/OneDrive/Local, replace this with the matching download node (Local File Trigger already provides the binary).

nodes.name: Only Images
nodes.notes: Skips PDFs, spreadsheets and anything else dropped into the folder.

nodes.name: Encode Base64
nodes.notes: Converts the binary image into base64 JSON for the ingest endpoint.

nodes.name: POST /api/ingest
nodes.notes: One call runs the whole pipeline server-side: AI extraction → mill resolution → Supabase Storage upload → fabric upsert → extraction log → similarity recalculation. Set TEXTILE_LIBRARY_URL (e.g. https://your-app.vercel.app) and N8N_WEBHOOK_SECRET (must match the app's env) in n8n environment variables. The endpoint responds 422 MILL_NOT_RESOLVED when the mill on the hanger can't be matched — those errors land in the failure branch.

nodes.name: Notify Staff (Email)

parameters.subject: =Fabric needs review: {{ $json.fabric.fabric_code }} ({{ Math.round($json.extraction.confidence_score) }}% confidence)

nodes.notes: Swap for a Slack / Teams / Telegram node if preferred — the IF node output is the only contract.
